summary: Deliver a browser-based veterinary-themed block-coding puzzle game with shared runtime logic, polished React UI, and a Node/SQLite telemetry backend plus analytics views.

implementation_roles.name: Shared Runtime & Content Engineer
implementation_roles.goal: Model the puzzle data pack and reusable execution/runtime logic that both app tiers consume.
notes: Deliver JSON-defined 17-level progression, failure hint rules, and reusable interpreter/state machine shared by frontend/backend.

implementation_roles.name: Frontend Experience & Workspace Engineer
implementation_roles.goal: Build the React/TypeScript client with draggable workspace, puzzle scenes, UI polish, and analytics views.
notes: Implements block workspace, scene renderer, feedback loop, code-view toggle, telemetry client buffers, and analytics UI pulling backend data.

implementation_roles.name: Backend Telemetry & Analytics Engineer
implementation_roles.goal: Implement Node/Express APIs, SQLite schema, event ingestion, analytics queries, and movement replay endpoints.
notes: Owns persistent telemetry storage, reports, replay endpoints, and ensures schema matches mandated tables.

global_constraints: Maintain exactly 17 data-driven puzzles covering sequencing, loops, and conditionals with JSON configuration.
Workspace must present command library on the left, on-start-root assembly on the right, and show Oops + hint on failure.
Execution engine must compile block graph to deterministic instructions with grid-based movement, loops, and conditionals.
SQLite database must implement all specified tables (users, sessions, puzzles, attempts, events, movements, puzzle_progress) and capture every gameplay/UI event including movement steps.
Provide analytics dashboards/pages capable of summarizing sessions, inspecting attempts, and replaying movement paths from stored data.
Frontend and backend must integrate to send/receive telemetry via HTTP endpoints and keep UI polished, accessible, and professional.
